questions.q: What did Dalio's failed bet on a Mexican default teach him?
a: To reason rationally rather than emotionally
To avoid making public predictions
To trust his instincts about markets
To keep his opinions away from employees
questions.why: Lesson 1 calls it his biggest failure and says it taught him to always think rationally, not emotionally.

questions.q: Why did Dalio lose everything even though his prediction was right?
a: Stocks and businesses soared instead of crashing
The Mexican government refused to pay him
His investors withdrew their money early
Regulators froze his fund during the crisis
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Mexico did default, but the expected crisis never came and markets rose against his bets.

questions.q: What is radical truthfulness meant to ensure inside a company?
a: Mistakes get raised, discussed and learned from
Every decision is made by a majority vote
Employees avoid saying anything hurtful
Managers keep sensitive data confidential
questions.why: Lesson 2 says honesty keeps errors from being swept away, so people can discuss and learn from them.

a: A place where the best ideas win
A company run by its longest-serving staff
A system where everyone gets an equal vote
A workplace where consensus is always required
questions.why: Lesson 3 defines an idea meritocracy as an environment where the strongest ideas rise to the top.

questions.q: How does Bridgewater judge which opinions to act on?
a: It scores people's believability on each issue
It holds a simple vote among all employees
It leaves the final call to Dalio alone
It follows whoever argues most forcefully
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the firm tracks people's views over time and weights decisions by credibility, not majority vote.
